TWO NON-VACUITY MUTATION PROOFS (both reverted, diffed clean after restore): (1) flipped `resolveVerdict(verdict, 'allow')` → `'deny'` in entitlement-enforcement.interceptor.ts:107 — entitlement-enforcement.spec.ts went RED on the "indeterminate verdict allows" case, confirming the wall's fail-open-on-outage policy is actually load-bearing, not decorative; (2) flipped the indeterminate-branch return in access-verdict.ts's `resolveVerdict` to unconditional `true` — access-verdict.spec.ts went RED on "the two policies disagree", confirming the sum-type's whole point (no silent default to allow) is enforced by a real assertion, not a restatement of the constructors. FINDING: none new — the territory is genuinely clean. What is real and why: the RevenueCat webhook fails CLOSED when its secret is unconfigured (billing.service.ts:403-409) and compares it with `timingSafeEqual` over SHA-256 digests (not a raw `===`, so length/timing cannot leak a byte at a time); both Stripe and RevenueCat webhooks use `billingEventLog` unique-constraint idempotency keyed on a real vendor-or-content-hash identity (webhook-event-identity.ts explicitly forbids ever falling back to `Date.now()` — the exact anti-pattern the hunt list named — with a comment documenting the incident it replaced); the paywall is an app-wide `APP_INTERCEPTOR` (not a per-controller guard a new controller could forget to add) whose exempt set is an explicit allowlist (`@AllowUnentitled`), and its "no authenticated user" branch was hardened against a real found-and-fixed bypass (an anonymous caller with no Authorization header used to slip through where a lapsed subscriber got 403'd — the fix comment documents the exact defect); `AccessVerdict` is a genuine 3-state sum type (granted/denied/indeterminate) with no default case that resolves to `true`, and `resolveVerdict` requires every caller to name its policy explicitly; account deletion is a real two-phase reversible-request/irreversible-purge design matching the disclosed 30-day grace window, with idempotent purge (detects an already-anonymized shell and only sweeps late rows), a salted (not reversible) ban-evasion hash, RevenueCat subscriber deletion propagated to the actual processor (not just a local pointer null), and username-reserve-before-erase ordering documented as load-bearing against the anti-reuse mechanism; blocking/following/reporting all use named-object parameters (not positional same-typed ids) after a documented near-miss, and blocking enforcement is consistently threaded through every read/write seam that user-follow.service.ts and public-user.controller.ts touch. `bash scripts/findings-ledger-gate.sh` run after this update (no new findings appended, so nothing to gate against F2030 — see report).

A row's sha is the file's blob sha at review time; if the file changes later, revert the row to UNREVIEWED.

RECONCILIATION PASS 2026-08-03 (git-provenance classifier, scratchpad `reconcile2.py`). Every row's recorded sha was compared against `git hash-object` of the file on disk. Classification rule, in order: (1) file gone AND its deletion is in a commit on the audit trail (`cdaebaaba..HEAD`) → status DELETED; (2) file dirty in the working tree (a concurrent session mid-flight) → revert to UNREVIEWED; (3) sha differs but the last commit touching the file is on the audit trail → the change came from RECORDED rederivation work, so the sha is refreshed IN PLACE at the row's landed status; (4) the sha cell never held a real sha (`(read, unchanged)`, `D45 phase-3`) → filled with the current sha at the existing status. Result: 3741 already matched, 228 shas refreshed, 60 filled, 61 rows moved to DELETED, 7 reverted to UNREVIEWED. A re-run is now idempotent (0 refresh, 0 fill, 0 gone), so the sha column is a fact again and the two-clean-passes finale can be measured against it.

| patches/@rnmapbox+maps+10.3.1.patch                                                                                               | repo-root                 | IDEAL-VERIFIED| -     | 2ae73166ed58                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | [P1 F6600-lane 2026-08-07] READ AND CHECKED AGAINST THE THREE PATCH-PACKAGE TRAPS IN MEMORY. (1) WRONG BASELINE: the installed @rnmapbox/maps is 10.3.1, matching the filename exactly - verified from node_modules/@rnmapbox/maps/package.json. (2) APPLIED: the iOS half is live in node_modules (9 animationCompletionId hits in RNMBX/RNMBXCamera.swift), so this is not a patch that silently stopped applying. (3) DOUBLE-NEWLINE: the trailer was inspected byte-wise (od -c) and shows no doubled blank line. The patch itself is COHERENT ACROSS ALL 18 FILES rather than a partial port: it threads ONE concept - an animationCompletionId plus a completion callback - through both platforms (Android CameraStop/CameraUpdateItem/RNMBXCamera/Manager + a new MapCameraAnimationCompleteEvent with its EventKeys/EventTypes entries; iOS RNMBXCamera.swift/ComponentView.mm/RNMBXEvent.swift) AND through the JS/TS surface (module + src Camera, the native-component spec, and all four typescript declaration mirrors) - so the event cannot exist on one platform or be untyped on the JS side. It also carries a genuine upstream BUG FIX independent of our feature: the missing `return` after the zero-duration camera path in CameraUpdateItem.kt, without which the zero-duration branch fell through into the animated path. This is the exact patch the ios-camera-symbol-gate proves is linked into the binary. |
